annotation.kind: source-faithful matrix-certificate form of Theorem 3.2 and formula (3.3)

assumptions: The symmetric inverse matrices S and Sinv represent W^(1/2) and W^(-1/2) from the paper's weighted Frobenius norm.
The two inverse identities explicitly encode the relation between W^(1/2) and W^(-1/2).
The orthogonal matrix Q and real function lambda give the source spectral decomposition of S*A*S.
The squared weighted Frobenius objective has exactly the same minimizers as the weighted Frobenius norm in equation (1.2).

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p40_t3_weighted_psd_projection (n A S Sinv Q lambda hSsymm hSinvSymm hSInv hInvS hQtQ hQQt hSpectral) : let X := weightedPsdProjection; X.PosSemidef and X globally minimizes weighted Frobenius square over every PSD Z and diag(A) <= diag(X)
formal_statement.plain_language: The eigenvalue-clipping formula (3.3) produces a positive semidefinite matrix that globally minimizes the weighted Frobenius distance to A, and every diagonal entry of the projection is at least the corresponding diagonal entry of A.

informal_proof: Use the spectral positive part of W^(1/2) A W^(1/2). Its congruence by W^(-1/2) is positive semidefinite. In spectral coordinates, clipping each eigenvalue at zero minimizes the squared Frobenius distance to every positive semidefinite competitor, including all nonnegative off-diagonal square terms. Transforming back gives weighted minimality. The congruence of the difference between the positive part and the original matrix is positive semidefinite, so its diagonal entries are nonnegative.
informal_statement: Prove Theorem 3.2's weighted positive-semidefinite projection formula and its diagonal inequality.

tier_rationale: The proof must establish orthogonal invariance of the Frobenius square, transport arbitrary PSD competitors into spectral coordinates, prove scalar clipping optimality and aggregate it against every off-diagonal matrix entry, transport the global weighted minimization back through two congruences, and derive diagonal monotonicity from a separate PSD difference. This is substantial multi-stage formalization, is not discharged by Mathlib imports, and has no corresponding compiled NumStability result, so L receives no material advantage over N.
